top_news.title: SingHealth Launches Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation in Pursuit of a Healthier World
top_news.summary: Initiated by SingHealth, this international alliance aims to enable people to live healthier, longer lives by advancing population health research, innovation and implementation across health systems worldwide. SINGAPORE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In pursuit of a vision to enable people to live healthier lives globally, SingHealth has launched the Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation, an international collaboration that brings together 14 leading healthcare, academic and research institutions from Asia, Europe, North America and Oceania to advance population health and improve health span. Mr Ong Ye Kung, Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health, Singapore (centre), officiating the launch of the Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation alongside representatives of the 14 co-founding member institutions. Initiated and hosted by SingHealth, this Alliance aims to foster collaborative research, accelerate the translation of research insights into action, develop a pipeline of population health leaders, and strengthen international efforts to tackle some of the world's most pressing health challenges stemming from ageing populations including the increasing burden of chronic diseases, health inequities and social determinants of health that adversely influence health outcomes across communities. This Alliance was officially launched at the opening ceremony of the inaugural Global Population Health Conference 2026 in Singapore at the Ngee Ann Kongsi Auditorium, Academia, on the Singapore General Hospital (SGH) Campus. Helping People Live Healthier, Longer Lives Healthcare challenges transcend geographical boundaries. Across the world, people are living longer but may spend a significant period with ill health. This results in significant pressure on healthcare resources, especially as climate change, workforce changes and evolving societal needs are creating new and increasingly complex health challenges. Many of these challenges extend beyond clinical care delivery and are shaped by the conditions and environment in which people live, learn, work and age. The Global Alliance seeks to address these issues through a strong shared commitment to improve population health by enabling individuals to lead not just long but healthy, active and independent lives for as long as possible. A Global Platform for Collaboration and Action The Global Alliance extends to the international stage, the work that is already underway within SingHealth's population health efforts over the last decade. The Alliance has six key focus areas: Fostering multi-national and inter-disciplinary research that address population health challenges; Developing shared measurement frameworks and evaluation approaches; Designing, testing and scaling of evidence-based care models across different healthcare systems; Jointly contributing to publications to advance global knowledge and practice; Enhancing international knowledge exchange and capacity building in population health; Shaping healthcare policy and implementation globally through developing evidence-based recommendations on key population health issues. By connecting leading health systems and research institutions across continents, the Alliance ensures that population health efforts are accelerated through close collaborations, undergirded by evidence-based research and experience, as well as enabling successful innovations to be developed locally for adaptation or implemented internationally. A distinguishing feature of the Alliance is its strong focus on scaling and implementation of successful pilot programmes and initiatives to benefit a larger community. Beyond generating new knowledge, members will work together to translate and contextualise evidence into real-world solutions through multidisciplinary collaborations, community living laboratories, capacity building initiatives, and practical implementation strategies that can be adopted across diverse settings. This approach ensures that interventions implemented are adapted to suit the local context for greater acceptance and efficacy, accelerating the adoption of proven approaches that improve health outcomes and reduce disparities across populations. Building a Global Community of Population Health Leaders The Alliance will also invest in developing the next generation of population health leaders through training, mentorship, academic exchanges and collaborative learning opportunities. One such initiative is the SingHealth Duke-NUS Academic Medical Centre and Duke University Population Health Research Initiative Grant, or SPRING. Launched in 2025, SPRING saw three members of the Alliance, namely Duke-NUS Medical School, Duke University and SingHealth, come together to offer mentoring programmes for early-career population health researchers. As the programme matures, SPRING is looking to expand and support mid-career investigators with demonstrated research potential in population health and health services research by providing research funding and opportunities for international collaboration to accelerate their development as independent researchers. 25 population health researchers have benefited from the programme and are on course to become research thought leaders in population health. Advancing Knowledge to Future-Proof Healthcare Systems One of the Alliance's first collaborative initiatives is an upcoming publication of a special issue in the journal Public Health. Themed "Future-Proofing Healthcare Systems", this special issue seeks to expand the growing body of literature on how population health approaches can support sustainable healthcare systems amid rapid population ageing and increasing healthcare complexity. Topics explored include AI-enabled healthcare workforces, precision and predictive health, community living laboratories, health economics and integrated approaches to chronic disease management. The issue is expected to be published in 2027. Professor Lesley Curtis, Chair of Population Health Sciences, Duke University School of Medicine, USA, said: "Population health challenges may manifest differently across countries, but many of their underlying drivers are remarkably similar. That is why global collaboration is so valuable. The Global Alliance brings together leading institutions with complementary expertise and diverse perspectives, creating opportunities to compare approaches, share lessons learned and co-develop solutions that can be adapted across uniquely local settings. We look forward to working with fellow members of the Global Alliance to advance research, strengthen implementation, and generate new knowledge that helps health systems better support the populations they serve." Celebrating SingHealth's Population Health Journey The Global Population Health Conference 2026 also serves as an occasion to celebrate key milestones in SingHealth's population health journey at home. On the sidelines of the conference today, SingHealth and the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) also marked the renewal of their longstanding Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), reaffirming their shared commitment to workforce development and interprofessional education. The renewed MOU will see new faculty appointments support collaborative educational programmes and knowledge exchange between both institutions, strengthening the pipeline of healthcare and social service professionals equipped to deliver person-centred, community-based care. The conference will also commemorate the 10th anniversary of ESTHER Network Singapore on Day 2 (24 November 2026). ESTHER Network Singapore was established in 2016 with the guidance and strong support from Region Jnkping County in Sweden, and has championed person-centredness in care delivery, embedding the perspectives of patients and caregivers into how care is designed and delivered across the health system. A decade on, its impact is reflected in more compassionate, responsive and integrated care experiences for patients across the SingHealth network. Together, these milestones reflect the depth and breadth of SingHealth's commitment to population health not just on the global stage, but in the communities it serves every day. Professor Lee Chien Earn, Deputy Group CEO (Regional Health System), SingHealth, said: "Around the world, healthcare systems face many similar challenges from rapidly ageing populations and a shrinking workforce, to the rising burden of chronic diseases that put increasing pressure on care delivery. No single country or institution can address these challenges alone. By bringing together leading experts from around the world, the Alliance allows us to leverage our diversity to synergise our unique strengths, test what works in different populations, and scale proven solutions at pace. Ultimately, this is about enabling people not just in Singapore, but globally, to live healthier and longer lives, in a sustainable way". He added: "This conference is also a moment for us to reflect on and celebrate the work we have been doing closer to home from a decade of ESTHER Network Singapore putting patients and caregivers at the heart of care, to our longstanding partnership with SUSS in developing the healthcare workforce of tomorrow and strengthening social-health integration. These efforts remind us that global ambitions must always be grounded in local action and human connection." About SingHealth SingHealth, Singapore's largest and leading public healthcare cluster, puts patients at the heart of all we do. Through our network of acute hospitals, national specialty centres, polyclinics and community hospitals, SingHealth delivers integrated care across every stage of life, from prevention and diagnosis to treatment, rehabilitation and long-term health management, offering multidisciplinary expertise across a wide range of specialties. Beyond hospital walls, SingHealth partners community care providers to enable the population to keep well, get well and live well. As an academic medical centre, SingHealth partners Duke-NUS Medical School and forms strategic collaborations across industries and the academia to advance research, innovation and education. Our goal is to drive impactful care outcomes, enhance patient experience and transform healthcare delivery, here and on the global front. For more information, please visit: www.singhealth.com.sg Members of the SingHealth group Hospitals (Tertiary Specialty Care): Singapore General Hospital, Changi General Hospital, Sengkang General Hospital, KK Women's and Children's Hospital, and Eastern General Hospital (expected completion around 2029 to 2030) National Specialty Centres (Tertiary Specialty Care): National Cancer Centre Singapore, National Dental Centre Singapore, National Heart Centre Singapore, National Neuroscience Institute, and Singapore National Eye Centre SingHealth Polyclinics (Primary Care): Bedok, Bukit Merah, Eunos, Marine Parade, Outram, Pasir Ris, Punggol, Sengkang, Tampines, Tampines North and Kaki Bukit (upcoming) SingHealth Community Hospitals (Intermediate and Long-term Care): Sengkang Community Hospital, Outram Community Hospital, and Eastern Community Hospital (expected completion around 2029 to 2030) ANNEX Co-founding Member Institutions of the Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation The Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation was established by the following 14 co-founding institutions: Duke University Duke-NUS Medical School Flinders University Knowledge Translation Program, Li Ka Shing Knowledge Institute of St. Michael's Hospital, Unity Health Toronto Leiden University Medical Center Region Jnkping County School of Public Health, Graduate School of Medicine, Kyoto University Singapore Health Services Pte Ltd (SingHealth) The Chinese University of Hong Kong The Governors of The University of Alberta The University of Sheffield University College London University Health Network West China School of Medicine and West China Hospital, Sichuan University

top_news.title: Invivyd Announces Positive DECLARATION Trial Data for Monoclonal Antibody VYD2311, and Ushers in a New Era for Immunization
top_news.summary: VYD2311 (ibramvibart) achieved high, durable antiviral activity predictive of 70-90% protection from symptomatic COVID-19 infection for both single- and multi-dose intramuscular arms Highly attractive safety and tolerability profile observed for single- and multi-dose VYD2311 arms, supporting broad population usePositive dialogue with U.S. FDA and HHS leadership has resulted in progress toward regulatory consistency between Invivyd monoclonal antibodies and related vaccines (e.g., COVID-19). Based on FDA feedback, upon planned VYD2311 BLA submission, Invivyd anticipates review for accelerated approval either by, or with input from, CBERInvivyd anticipates submitting a BLA based on DECLARATION and LIBERTY data to FDA in Q1 2027Investor call to be held at 8:30 am EST on November 23, 2026 NEW HAVEN, Conn., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Invivyd, Inc. (Nasdaq: IVVD) today announced all interim analysis primary and secondary endpoints were met in the DECLARATION Phase 3 trial of VYD2311 (ibramvibart). VYD2311, administered via intramuscular injection (IM), demonstrated high and durable antiviral activity, consistent with Invivyd’s target 70-90% protection from RT-PCR confirmed symptomatic COVID-19, versus placebo. VYD2311 demonstrated an overall highly attractive safety and tolerability profile in both single- and multi-dose arms. Invivyd intends to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) seeking accelerated approval of VYD2311 for the prevention of symptomatic COVID-19 based on the positive interim analysis of the Phase 3 DECLARATION trial and the supportive data from the Phase 3 LIBERTY trial comparing VYD2311 and an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.

top_news.title: SinoUnited Health Hosts International Medical Forum, Spotlighting Shanghai as a Rising Global Medical Destination
top_news.summary: SHANGHAI, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As Shanghai strengthens its position as an international medical hub,SinoUnited Health, a leading private healthcare provider headquartered in Shanghai, hosted its 2026 International Medical Forum on November 13. Marking the organization's 10th anniversary, the forum highlighted a decade of clinical development, international collaboration and patient-centered healthcare innovation. Held under the theme "China Innovation in Global Healthcare," the forum brought together medical experts and healthcare industry representatives from China and abroad to discuss advances in cancer treatment, pan-vascular disease treatment, longevity medicine and AI-driven healthcare. It also explored how China's growing clinical expertise, combined with international medical experience, can create new opportunities for high-quality, coordinated care for patients from around the world. Building Trust Through Clinical Excellence and a Seamless Patient Experience At the forum, Dr. Kathy Shi, Founder and CEO of SinoUnited Health and President of Shanghai SinoUnited Hospital, identified trust as a defining factor in cross-border healthcare. For patients seeking treatment overseas, particularly those facing serious or complex conditions, choosing where to receive care is a significant decision. Building confidence requires more than clinical expertise alone: it depends on transparent communication, coordinated services and continuity of care. This starts with access to experienced physicians, evidence-based clinical guidelines, advanced medical technologies and appropriate treatment options. Patients also need a clear understanding of their condition and treatment plan, with decisions made through open communication with their physicians. For international patients, bilingual medical teams, dedicated care coordination and concierge services help simplify the process of navigating an unfamiliar healthcare system. Digital platforms can further support continuity of care, allowing patients and their medical teams in their home countries to maintain follow-up across borders. Over the past decade, SinoUnited Health has developed its clinical capabilities and healthcare network by combining international medical experience with local clinical resources, supported by ongoing exchanges with leading medical institutions in China and abroad. Its physician-led "General practitioner + Specialist" model connects primary care with specialist expertise, helping patients navigate the full care journey, from initial assessment and diagnosis to treatment and follow-up. The forum highlighted how this approach is being applied across its specialty areas, including advanced cancer treatment, pan-vascular disease management and longevity medicine. Expanding Access to Advanced Cancer Treatment One of the clinical updates at the forum came from SinoUnited Health's International CAR-T Cell Therapy Center. As of October 2026, the center has conducted more than 150 consultations with patients from around the world and completed over 40 CAR-T treatments since its establishment. Most treated patients achieved complete remission, with patients from 13 countries and regions, including New Zealand, Canada, Singapore and Thailand. Behind these results is a coordinated care model that brings together specialists in hematology, cardiology, gastroenterology, neurology and radiology, alongside the hospital's inpatient team. The center also coordinates access to clinical resources at leading Grade A tertiary hospitals in China, as well as international experts, helping patients navigate complex treatment decisions and access specialized care. Beyond hematological malignancies, the forum also examined China's growing contribution to the diagnosis and treatment of solid tumors. Professor Shen Baiyong, Vice President of Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, shared clinical developments in pancreatic cancer, covering early diagnosis, surgical treatment and comprehensive disease management. With a large patient population, expanding clinical research capacity and continued advances in medical technology, China is generating valuable real-world experience in cancer care. Clinical insights from the country's experience in managing complex diseases such as pancreatic cancer can contribute to the wider medical community's understanding of diagnosis and treatment. For SinoUnited Health, bringing together specialist expertise, multidisciplinary teams and access to the latest treatment options is essential to delivering high-quality care and optimizing treatment outcomes. The forum also marked the launch of the SinoUnited Health Women's Health Center Cancer Survivorship Program. Building on the center's experience in women's health and breast cancer screening, the program extends support beyond active treatment. Its focus includes recurrence monitoring, lifestyle interventions, psychological support and the management of longer-term health concerns, addressing the needs of women as they transition into survivorship. Pan-Vascular Model for International Second Opinion Service Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain major global health challenges. At the forum, Professor Ge Junbo, Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Director of Cardiology at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, delivered a keynote presentation on the challenges and future of pan-vascular disease management. He emphasized the importance of moving beyond fragmented, single-specialty care toward integrated risk assessment, early screening and multidisciplinary management, with a focus on shared risk factors such as hypertension, dyslipidemia and diabetes. Putting this approach into practice, SinoUnited Health launched its International Pan-Vascular Second Opinion Service earlier in October, giving international patients a structured way to access specialist opinions and coordinated medical resources in China. The service covers four areas: cardiovascular diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, peripheral vascular diseases, and metabolic and systemic health risks. Its care pathway includes medical record review, remote multidisciplinary consultations, coordination of in-person appointments, English-language post-treatment reports, cross-border medical information exchange and remote follow-up supported by wearable devices after patients return home. By connecting expert assessment in China with follow-up across borders, the service aims to help patients make informed treatment decisions while maintaining continuity of care beyond their visit. Longevity Medicine and Preventive Healthcare Beyond Treatment As healthcare places greater emphasis on prevention and healthy aging, SinoUnited Health is extending its focus beyond treating existing conditions to identifying health risks earlier and supporting long-term well-being. At the forum, experts from Mayo Clinic shared perspectives on translating aging science into clinical practice, highlighting the importance of healthspan - the years lived in good health - alongside lifespan. Their discussions explored the role of multidisciplinary assessment and evidence-based interventions, including exercise, nutrition, sleep, preventive screening and social connection. Dr. Lily Yan, SinoUnited Health Group Vice President, presented the organization's approach to longevity medicine. Grounded in evidence-based medicine and multidisciplinary collaboration, the model combines comprehensive health assessments, advanced testing, personalized intervention plans and ongoing monitoring. Rather than relying on isolated tests or individual health indicators, the approach focuses on identifying and managing a range of health risks, including cardiovascular disease, cognitive decline, cancer, metabolic disorders and impaired cardiopulmonary function. The newly inaugurated New Bund Longevity Center provides a dedicated setting for coordinated assessments, preventive interventions and long-term health management. Digital Health Extending Care Beyond Hospital Visits For international patients, particularly those who live outside China or return home after treatment, maintaining continuity of care can be challenging. SinoUnited Health is addressing this through digital health platforms and a combination of online and in-person services designed to connect different stages of the patient journey. Through its digital health platform, the organization is working to bring together appointments, health records, examination results and follow-up services. Patients can access their health information over time, while medical teams can use digital tools to support ongoing monitoring and care coordination. The forum also highlighted SinoUnited Health's exploration of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in areas such as appointment scheduling, triage, examinations and follow-up. These initiatives form part of a broader effort to make healthcare more accessible and continuous, extending support beyond hospital visits and enabling patients to remain connected with their care teams even after returning to their home countries. "Over the past decade, we have continued to strengthen our medical capabilities while staying closely attuned to developments in global healthcare," said Dr. Kathy Shi. "We are committed to translating innovative medical concepts and technologies into clinical practice, and to working with healthcare institutions in China and internationally to explore new possibilities in patient-centered care." As SinoUnited Health enters its second decade, it will continue to advance its vision of "China Innovation in Global Healthcare," bringing together international medical experience, China's clinical expertise and integrated healthcare services to serve patients in Shanghai and beyond. About SinoUnited Health Established in 2016 and anchored in Shanghai,SinoUnited Health(SUH) is a high-quality private healthcare provider with the largest and most extensive medical network in the Yangtze River Delta Region. Upholding the concept of "Patient First," SUH provides trustworthy, cost-controllable, and high-quality healthcare services that meet both domestic and international standards. Its international medical team strictly follows evidence-based guidelines and maintains long-term collaboration with renowned medical institutions in China and abroad, ensuring patients receive reliable, world-class care. As a physician-driven institution,SUH's "General Practitioner+ Specialist" model offers holistic, professional, and personalized solutions, making premium private healthcare accessible for every family. For more information, please visit: www.suhhealth.com Contact: internationalcare@suh.cn

top_news.title: IIHM Signs Historic MoU with Club Med for Student Placement
top_news.summary: As hospitality increasingly becomes a globally interconnected profession, the opportunities available to young professionals extend far beyond national boundaries. A new collaboration between the International Institute of Hotel Management (IIHM) and Club Med seeks to strengthen this connection, creating a framework for international recruitment opportunities, industry engagement, professional training and career development for hospitality students. IIHM and Club Med have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) establishing a framework for industry-academia collaboration, international hospitality internships, hospitality graduate recruitment, professional training, talent development and career opportunities across the global hospitality industry. The collaboration brings hospitality education closer to international industry practice, creating avenues for students to explore global hospitality careers and international hospitality employment opportunities. The MoU was signed on behalf of IIHM by Mr Abdullah Ahmed, Chief Operating Officer , International Institute of Hotel Management, and on behalf of Club Med by Mr Sunil Kumar Koosul, Director of Human Resources (Welfare & Administration), Club Med Indian Ocean. The visiting Club Med delegation comprised Ms Souhasnee Sookun, Talent Acquisition Manager, Club Med Indian Ocean; Mr Sunil Kumar Koosul, Director of Human Resources (Welfare & Administration), Club Med Indian Ocean; and Mr Thomas Pierre Rodriguez, Director of Human Resources (Resorts), Club Med Indian Ocean. Connecting hospitality education with international career opportunities The partnership reflects the growing importance of aligning hospitality education with the expectations, standards and evolving needs of an increasingly international hospitality industry. For students entering the profession, exposure to global workplace cultures, guest expectations, service practices and international resort operations can be an important part of building a long-term career. The MoU creates a framework for students to explore international hospitality internships and recruitment opportunities while gaining exposure to professional environments shaped by diverse cultures, international guests and global service standards. Founded in 1950, Club Med operates more than 70 resorts across the world, along with two yachts, bringing together hospitality professionals from diverse cultural and geographical backgrounds. Its international operations offer a distinctive environment in which hospitality professionals develop their skills through guest interaction, teamwork, operational experience and exposure to multicultural workplaces. The collaboration is expected to facilitate engagement through professional interactions, guest lectures, masterclasses, workshops, mentoring initiatives, resort visits and other activities that bring industry experience into the educational environment. International recruitment and the future of hospitality careers As part of the recruitment engagement emerging through the collaboration, opportunities for IIHM students are being explored across South Africa, Seychelles and Mauritius, offering students the possibility of experiencing hospitality operations in international resort destinations. For aspiring hospitality professionals, international exposure is about more than geographical mobility. It is about learning to work with guests from different cultures, adapting to diverse service expectations, developing confidence in professional environments and understanding hospitality as a truly global profession. articles.title: SingHealth Launches Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation in Pursuit of a Healthier World
articles.summary: Initiated by SingHealth, this international alliance aims to enable people to live healthier, longer lives by advancing population health research, innovation and implementation across health systems worldwide. SINGAPORE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In pursuit of a vision to enable people to live healthier lives globally, SingHealth has launched the Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation, an international collaboration that brings together 14 leading healthcare, academic and research institutions from Asia, Europe, North America and Oceania to advance population health and improve health span. Mr Ong Ye Kung, Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health, Singapore (centre), officiating the launch of the Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation alongside representatives of the 14 co-founding member institutions. Initiated and hosted by SingHealth, this Alliance aims to foster collaborative research, accelerate the translation of research insights into action, develop a pipeline of population health leaders, and strengthen international efforts to tackle some of the world's most pressing health challenges stemming from ageing populations including the increasing burden of chronic diseases, health inequities and social determinants of health that adversely influence health outcomes across communities. This Alliance was officially launched at the opening ceremony of the inaugural Global Population Health Conference 2026 in Singapore at the Ngee Ann Kongsi Auditorium, Academia, on the Singapore General Hospital (SGH) Campus. Helping People Live Healthier, Longer Lives Healthcare challenges transcend geographical boundaries. Across the world, people are living longer but may spend a significant period with ill health. This results in significant pressure on healthcare resources, especially as climate change, workforce changes and evolving societal needs are creating new and increasingly complex health challenges. Many of these challenges extend beyond clinical care delivery and are shaped by the conditions and environment in which people live, learn, work and age. The Global Alliance seeks to address these issues through a strong shared commitment to improve population health by enabling individuals to lead not just long but healthy, active and independent lives for as long as possible. A Global Platform for Collaboration and Action The Global Alliance extends to the international stage, the work that is already underway within SingHealth's population health efforts over the last decade. The Alliance has six key focus areas: Fostering multi-national and inter-disciplinary research that address population health challenges; Developing shared measurement frameworks and evaluation approaches; Designing, testing and scaling of evidence-based care models across different healthcare systems; Jointly contributing to publications to advance global knowledge and practice; Enhancing international knowledge exchange and capacity building in population health; Shaping healthcare policy and implementation globally through developing evidence-based recommendations on key population health issues. By connecting leading health systems and research institutions across continents, the Alliance ensures that population health efforts are accelerated through close collaborations, undergirded by evidence-based research and experience, as well as enabling successful innovations to be developed locally for adaptation or implemented internationally. A distinguishing feature of the Alliance is its strong focus on scaling and implementation of successful pilot programmes and initiatives to benefit a larger community. Beyond generating new knowledge, members will work together to translate and contextualise evidence into real-world solutions through multidisciplinary collaborations, community living laboratories, capacity building initiatives, and practical implementation strategies that can be adopted across diverse settings. This approach ensures that interventions implemented are adapted to suit the local context for greater acceptance and efficacy, accelerating the adoption of proven approaches that improve health outcomes and reduce disparities across populations. Building a Global Community of Population Health Leaders The Alliance will also invest in developing the next generation of population health leaders through training, mentorship, academic exchanges and collaborative learning opportunities. One such initiative is the SingHealth Duke-NUS Academic Medical Centre and Duke University Population Health Research Initiative Grant, or SPRING. Launched in 2025, SPRING saw three members of the Alliance, namely Duke-NUS Medical School, Duke University and SingHealth, come together to offer mentoring programmes for early-career population health researchers. As the programme matures, SPRING is looking to expand and support mid-career investigators with demonstrated research potential in population health and health services research by providing research funding and opportunities for international collaboration to accelerate their development as independent researchers. 25 population health researchers have benefited from the programme and are on course to become research thought leaders in population health. Advancing Knowledge to Future-Proof Healthcare Systems One of the Alliance's first collaborative initiatives is an upcoming publication of a special issue in the journal Public Health. Themed "Future-Proofing Healthcare Systems", this special issue seeks to expand the growing body of literature on how population health approaches can support sustainable healthcare systems amid rapid population ageing and increasing healthcare complexity. Topics explored include AI-enabled healthcare workforces, precision and predictive health, community living laboratories, health economics and integrated approaches to chronic disease management. The issue is expected to be published in 2027. Professor Lesley Curtis, Chair of Population Health Sciences, Duke University School of Medicine, USA, said: "Population health challenges may manifest differently across countries, but many of their underlying drivers are remarkably similar. That is why global collaboration is so valuable. The Global Alliance brings together leading institutions with complementary expertise and diverse perspectives, creating opportunities to compare approaches, share lessons learned and co-develop solutions that can be adapted across uniquely local settings. We look forward to working with fellow members of the Global Alliance to advance research, strengthen implementation, and generate new knowledge that helps health systems better support the populations they serve." Celebrating SingHealth's Population Health Journey The Global Population Health Conference 2026 also serves as an occasion to celebrate key milestones in SingHealth's population health journey at home. On the sidelines of the conference today, SingHealth and the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) also marked the renewal of their longstanding Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), reaffirming their shared commitment to workforce development and interprofessional education. The renewed MOU will see new faculty appointments support collaborative educational programmes and knowledge exchange between both institutions, strengthening the pipeline of healthcare and social service professionals equipped to deliver person-centred, community-based care. The conference will also commemorate the 10th anniversary of ESTHER Network Singapore on Day 2 (24 November 2026). ESTHER Network Singapore was established in 2016 with the guidance and strong support from Region Jnkping County in Sweden, and has championed person-centredness in care delivery, embedding the perspectives of patients and caregivers into how care is designed and delivered across the health system. A decade on, its impact is reflected in more compassionate, responsive and integrated care experiences for patients across the SingHealth network. Together, these milestones reflect the depth and breadth of SingHealth's commitment to population health not just on the global stage, but in the communities it serves every day. Professor Lee Chien Earn, Deputy Group CEO (Regional Health System), SingHealth, said: "Around the world, healthcare systems face many similar challenges from rapidly ageing populations and a shrinking workforce, to the rising burden of chronic diseases that put increasing pressure on care delivery. No single country or institution can address these challenges alone. By bringing together leading experts from around the world, the Alliance allows us to leverage our diversity to synergise our unique strengths, test what works in different populations, and scale proven solutions at pace. Ultimately, this is about enabling people not just in Singapore, but globally, to live healthier and longer lives, in a sustainable way". He added: "This conference is also a moment for us to reflect on and celebrate the work we have been doing closer to home from a decade of ESTHER Network Singapore putting patients and caregivers at the heart of care, to our longstanding partnership with SUSS in developing the healthcare workforce of tomorrow and strengthening social-health integration. These efforts remind us that global ambitions must always be grounded in local action and human connection." About SingHealth SingHealth, Singapore's largest and leading public healthcare cluster, puts patients at the heart of all we do. Through our network of acute hospitals, national specialty centres, polyclinics and community hospitals, SingHealth delivers integrated care across every stage of life, from prevention and diagnosis to treatment, rehabilitation and long-term health management, offering multidisciplinary expertise across a wide range of specialties. Beyond hospital walls, SingHealth partners community care providers to enable the population to keep well, get well and live well. As an academic medical centre, SingHealth partners Duke-NUS Medical School and forms strategic collaborations across industries and the academia to advance research, innovation and education. Our goal is to drive impactful care outcomes, enhance patient experience and transform healthcare delivery, here and on the global front. For more information, please visit: www.singhealth.com.sg Members of the SingHealth group Hospitals (Tertiary Specialty Care): Singapore General Hospital, Changi General Hospital, Sengkang General Hospital, KK Women's and Children's Hospital, and Eastern General Hospital (expected completion around 2029 to 2030) National Specialty Centres (Tertiary Specialty Care): National Cancer Centre Singapore, National Dental Centre Singapore, National Heart Centre Singapore, National Neuroscience Institute, and Singapore National Eye Centre SingHealth Polyclinics (Primary Care): Bedok, Bukit Merah, Eunos, Marine Parade, Outram, Pasir Ris, Punggol, Sengkang, Tampines, Tampines North and Kaki Bukit (upcoming) SingHealth Community Hospitals (Intermediate and Long-term Care): Sengkang Community Hospital, Outram Community Hospital, and Eastern Community Hospital (expected completion around 2029 to 2030) ANNEX Co-founding Member Institutions of the Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation The Global Alliance for Population Health Research and Implementation was established by the following 14 co-founding institutions: Duke University Duke-NUS Medical School Flinders University Knowledge Translation Program, Li Ka Shing Knowledge Institute of St. Michael's Hospital, Unity Health Toronto Leiden University Medical Center Region Jnkping County School of Public Health, Graduate School of Medicine, Kyoto University Singapore Health Services Pte Ltd (SingHealth) The Chinese University of Hong Kong The Governors of The University of Alberta The University of Sheffield University College London University Health Network West China School of Medicine and West China Hospital, Sichuan University

articles.title: Invivyd Announces Positive DECLARATION Trial Data for Monoclonal Antibody VYD2311, and Ushers in a New Era for Immunization
articles.summary: VYD2311 (ibramvibart) achieved high, durable antiviral activity predictive of 70-90% protection from symptomatic COVID-19 infection for both single- and multi-dose intramuscular arms Highly attractive safety and tolerability profile observed for single- and multi-dose VYD2311 arms, supporting broad population usePositive dialogue with U.S. FDA and HHS leadership has resulted in progress toward regulatory consistency between Invivyd monoclonal antibodies and related vaccines (e.g., COVID-19). Based on FDA feedback, upon planned VYD2311 BLA submission, Invivyd anticipates review for accelerated approval either by, or with input from, CBERInvivyd anticipates submitting a BLA based on DECLARATION and LIBERTY data to FDA in Q1 2027Investor call to be held at 8:30 am EST on November 23, 2026 NEW HAVEN, Conn., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Invivyd, Inc. (Nasdaq: IVVD) today announced all interim analysis primary and secondary endpoints were met in the DECLARATION Phase 3 trial of VYD2311 (ibramvibart). VYD2311, administered via intramuscular injection (IM), demonstrated high and durable antiviral activity, consistent with Invivyd’s target 70-90% protection from RT-PCR confirmed symptomatic COVID-19, versus placebo. VYD2311 demonstrated an overall highly attractive safety and tolerability profile in both single- and multi-dose arms. Invivyd intends to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) seeking accelerated approval of VYD2311 for the prevention of symptomatic COVID-19 based on the positive interim analysis of the Phase 3 DECLARATION trial and the supportive data from the Phase 3 LIBERTY trial comparing VYD2311 and an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.

articles.title: SinoUnited Health Hosts International Medical Forum, Spotlighting Shanghai as a Rising Global Medical Destination
articles.summary: SHANGHAI, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As Shanghai strengthens its position as an international medical hub,SinoUnited Health, a leading private healthcare provider headquartered in Shanghai, hosted its 2026 International Medical Forum on November 13. Marking the organization's 10th anniversary, the forum highlighted a decade of clinical development, international collaboration and patient-centered healthcare innovation. Held under the theme "China Innovation in Global Healthcare," the forum brought together medical experts and healthcare industry representatives from China and abroad to discuss advances in cancer treatment, pan-vascular disease treatment, longevity medicine and AI-driven healthcare. It also explored how China's growing clinical expertise, combined with international medical experience, can create new opportunities for high-quality, coordinated care for patients from around the world. Building Trust Through Clinical Excellence and a Seamless Patient Experience At the forum, Dr. Kathy Shi, Founder and CEO of SinoUnited Health and President of Shanghai SinoUnited Hospital, identified trust as a defining factor in cross-border healthcare. For patients seeking treatment overseas, particularly those facing serious or complex conditions, choosing where to receive care is a significant decision. Building confidence requires more than clinical expertise alone: it depends on transparent communication, coordinated services and continuity of care. This starts with access to experienced physicians, evidence-based clinical guidelines, advanced medical technologies and appropriate treatment options. Patients also need a clear understanding of their condition and treatment plan, with decisions made through open communication with their physicians. For international patients, bilingual medical teams, dedicated care coordination and concierge services help simplify the process of navigating an unfamiliar healthcare system. Digital platforms can further support continuity of care, allowing patients and their medical teams in their home countries to maintain follow-up across borders. Over the past decade, SinoUnited Health has developed its clinical capabilities and healthcare network by combining international medical experience with local clinical resources, supported by ongoing exchanges with leading medical institutions in China and abroad. Its physician-led "General practitioner + Specialist" model connects primary care with specialist expertise, helping patients navigate the full care journey, from initial assessment and diagnosis to treatment and follow-up. The forum highlighted how this approach is being applied across its specialty areas, including advanced cancer treatment, pan-vascular disease management and longevity medicine. Expanding Access to Advanced Cancer Treatment One of the clinical updates at the forum came from SinoUnited Health's International CAR-T Cell Therapy Center. As of October 2026, the center has conducted more than 150 consultations with patients from around the world and completed over 40 CAR-T treatments since its establishment. Most treated patients achieved complete remission, with patients from 13 countries and regions, including New Zealand, Canada, Singapore and Thailand. Behind these results is a coordinated care model that brings together specialists in hematology, cardiology, gastroenterology, neurology and radiology, alongside the hospital's inpatient team. The center also coordinates access to clinical resources at leading Grade A tertiary hospitals in China, as well as international experts, helping patients navigate complex treatment decisions and access specialized care. Beyond hematological malignancies, the forum also examined China's growing contribution to the diagnosis and treatment of solid tumors. Professor Shen Baiyong, Vice President of Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, shared clinical developments in pancreatic cancer, covering early diagnosis, surgical treatment and comprehensive disease management. With a large patient population, expanding clinical research capacity and continued advances in medical technology, China is generating valuable real-world experience in cancer care. Clinical insights from the country's experience in managing complex diseases such as pancreatic cancer can contribute to the wider medical community's understanding of diagnosis and treatment. For SinoUnited Health, bringing together specialist expertise, multidisciplinary teams and access to the latest treatment options is essential to delivering high-quality care and optimizing treatment outcomes. The forum also marked the launch of the SinoUnited Health Women's Health Center Cancer Survivorship Program. Building on the center's experience in women's health and breast cancer screening, the program extends support beyond active treatment. Its focus includes recurrence monitoring, lifestyle interventions, psychological support and the management of longer-term health concerns, addressing the needs of women as they transition into survivorship. Pan-Vascular Model for International Second Opinion Service Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain major global health challenges. At the forum, Professor Ge Junbo, Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Director of Cardiology at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, delivered a keynote presentation on the challenges and future of pan-vascular disease management. He emphasized the importance of moving beyond fragmented, single-specialty care toward integrated risk assessment, early screening and multidisciplinary management, with a focus on shared risk factors such as hypertension, dyslipidemia and diabetes. Putting this approach into practice, SinoUnited Health launched its International Pan-Vascular Second Opinion Service earlier in October, giving international patients a structured way to access specialist opinions and coordinated medical resources in China. The service covers four areas: cardiovascular diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, peripheral vascular diseases, and metabolic and systemic health risks. Its care pathway includes medical record review, remote multidisciplinary consultations, coordination of in-person appointments, English-language post-treatment reports, cross-border medical information exchange and remote follow-up supported by wearable devices after patients return home. By connecting expert assessment in China with follow-up across borders, the service aims to help patients make informed treatment decisions while maintaining continuity of care beyond their visit. Longevity Medicine and Preventive Healthcare Beyond Treatment As healthcare places greater emphasis on prevention and healthy aging, SinoUnited Health is extending its focus beyond treating existing conditions to identifying health risks earlier and supporting long-term well-being. At the forum, experts from Mayo Clinic shared perspectives on translating aging science into clinical practice, highlighting the importance of healthspan - the years lived in good health - alongside lifespan. Their discussions explored the role of multidisciplinary assessment and evidence-based interventions, including exercise, nutrition, sleep, preventive screening and social connection. Dr. Lily Yan, SinoUnited Health Group Vice President, presented the organization's approach to longevity medicine. Grounded in evidence-based medicine and multidisciplinary collaboration, the model combines comprehensive health assessments, advanced testing, personalized intervention plans and ongoing monitoring. Rather than relying on isolated tests or individual health indicators, the approach focuses on identifying and managing a range of health risks, including cardiovascular disease, cognitive decline, cancer, metabolic disorders and impaired cardiopulmonary function. The newly inaugurated New Bund Longevity Center provides a dedicated setting for coordinated assessments, preventive interventions and long-term health management. Digital Health Extending Care Beyond Hospital Visits For international patients, particularly those who live outside China or return home after treatment, maintaining continuity of care can be challenging. SinoUnited Health is addressing this through digital health platforms and a combination of online and in-person services designed to connect different stages of the patient journey. Through its digital health platform, the organization is working to bring together appointments, health records, examination results and follow-up services. Patients can access their health information over time, while medical teams can use digital tools to support ongoing monitoring and care coordination. The forum also highlighted SinoUnited Health's exploration of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in areas such as appointment scheduling, triage, examinations and follow-up. These initiatives form part of a broader effort to make healthcare more accessible and continuous, extending support beyond hospital visits and enabling patients to remain connected with their care teams even after returning to their home countries. "Over the past decade, we have continued to strengthen our medical capabilities while staying closely attuned to developments in global healthcare," said Dr. Kathy Shi. "We are committed to translating innovative medical concepts and technologies into clinical practice, and to working with healthcare institutions in China and internationally to explore new possibilities in patient-centered care." As SinoUnited Health enters its second decade, it will continue to advance its vision of "China Innovation in Global Healthcare," bringing together international medical experience, China's clinical expertise and integrated healthcare services to serve patients in Shanghai and beyond. About SinoUnited Health Established in 2016 and anchored in Shanghai,SinoUnited Health(SUH) is a high-quality private healthcare provider with the largest and most extensive medical network in the Yangtze River Delta Region. Upholding the concept of "Patient First," SUH provides trustworthy, cost-controllable, and high-quality healthcare services that meet both domestic and international standards. Its international medical team strictly follows evidence-based guidelines and maintains long-term collaboration with renowned medical institutions in China and abroad, ensuring patients receive reliable, world-class care. As a physician-driven institution,SUH's "General Practitioner+ Specialist" model offers holistic, professional, and personalized solutions, making premium private healthcare accessible for every family. articles.title: IIHM Signs Historic MoU with Club Med for Student Placement
articles.summary: As hospitality increasingly becomes a globally interconnected profession, the opportunities available to young professionals extend far beyond national boundaries. A new collaboration between the International Institute of Hotel Management (IIHM) and Club Med seeks to strengthen this connection, creating a framework for international recruitment opportunities, industry engagement, professional training and career development for hospitality students. IIHM and Club Med have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) establishing a framework for industry-academia collaboration, international hospitality internships, hospitality graduate recruitment, professional training, talent development and career opportunities across the global hospitality industry. The collaboration brings hospitality education closer to international industry practice, creating avenues for students to explore global hospitality careers and international hospitality employment opportunities. The MoU was signed on behalf of IIHM by Mr Abdullah Ahmed, Chief Operating Officer , International Institute of Hotel Management, and on behalf of Club Med by Mr Sunil Kumar Koosul, Director of Human Resources (Welfare & Administration), Club Med Indian Ocean. The visiting Club Med delegation comprised Ms Souhasnee Sookun, Talent Acquisition Manager, Club Med Indian Ocean; Mr Sunil Kumar Koosul, Director of Human Resources (Welfare & Administration), Club Med Indian Ocean; and Mr Thomas Pierre Rodriguez, Director of Human Resources (Resorts), Club Med Indian Ocean. Connecting hospitality education with international career opportunities The partnership reflects the growing importance of aligning hospitality education with the expectations, standards and evolving needs of an increasingly international hospitality industry. For students entering the profession, exposure to global workplace cultures, guest expectations, service practices and international resort operations can be an important part of building a long-term career. The MoU creates a framework for students to explore international hospitality internships and recruitment opportunities while gaining exposure to professional environments shaped by diverse cultures, international guests and global service standards. Founded in 1950, Club Med operates more than 70 resorts across the world, along with two yachts, bringing together hospitality professionals from diverse cultural and geographical backgrounds. Its international operations offer a distinctive environment in which hospitality professionals develop their skills through guest interaction, teamwork, operational experience and exposure to multicultural workplaces. The collaboration is expected to facilitate engagement through professional interactions, guest lectures, masterclasses, workshops, mentoring initiatives, resort visits and other activities that bring industry experience into the educational environment. International recruitment and the future of hospitality careers As part of the recruitment engagement emerging through the collaboration, opportunities for IIHM students are being explored across South Africa, Seychelles and Mauritius, offering students the possibility of experiencing hospitality operations in international resort destinations. For aspiring hospitality professionals, international exposure is about more than geographical mobility. It is about learning to work with guests from different cultures, adapting to diverse service expectations, developing confidence in professional environments and understanding hospitality as a truly global profession.
